concepts.name: Vectors as arrows and lists
concepts.summary: Recognise a vector as both a geometric arrow and an ordered list of numbers, and read its components.

concepts.name: Vector addition and scaling
concepts.summary: Add vectors componentwise and multiply by scalars, and explain what each does geometrically.

concepts.name: Linear combinations
concepts.summary: Form and interpret sums of scaled vectors as new vectors reachable from given ones.

concepts.name: Matrices as rectangular arrays
concepts.summary: Identify matrix size, rows, columns and entries, and recognise special forms such as identity, zero and diagonal.

concepts.name: Matrix-vector product
concepts.summary: Compute Ax as a linear combination of the columns of A and as row-wise dot products.

concepts.name: Systems of linear equations
concepts.summary: Write a system of equations in matrix form Ax = b and explain what a solution means.

misconceptions.text: A vector is only an arrow and cannot be described by a list of numbers, or vice versa.
A matrix times a vector is computed by multiplying corresponding entries one by one.
A system of linear equations always has exactly one solution.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.summary: Apply elementary row operations to reduce an augmented matrix to echelon or reduced echelon form and solve the system.

concepts.name: Solution set types
concepts.summary: Use pivots and free variables to decide whether a system has no, one or infinitely many solutions and describe them parametrically.

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.summary: Multiply compatible matrices, check dimensions, and know that the product is generally not commutative.

concepts.name: Transpose and special matrices
concepts.summary: Compute transposes and recognise symmetric, triangular and diagonal matrices and the rule (AB)^T = B^T A^T.

concepts.name: Matrix inverse
concepts.summary: Find the inverse of a square matrix by row reducing [A | I] and use it to solve Ax = b.

concepts.name: Dot product and length
concepts.summary: Compute dot products, vector lengths and angles, and test whether two vectors are perpendicular.

concepts.name: Linear transformations as matrices
concepts.summary: Describe how a matrix rotates, scales, reflects or shears the plane and read the matrix from the images of basis vectors.

misconceptions.text: Matrix multiplication is commutative, so AB = BA.
Every square matrix has an inverse.
The inverse of a matrix is found by taking the reciprocal of each entry.

concepts.name: Linear independence
concepts.summary: Test whether vectors are independent by checking whether Ax = 0 has only the trivial solution.

concepts.name: Span and subspaces
concepts.summary: Determine the span of a set of vectors and verify whether a set is a subspace by closure under addition and scaling.

concepts.name: Basis and dimension
concepts.summary: Identify a basis of a subspace, find its dimension and express vectors in coordinates relative to it.

concepts.name: Null space and column space
concepts.summary: Compute bases for the null space and column space of a matrix and interpret them in terms of solutions and outputs.

concepts.name: Rank and rank-nullity
concepts.summary: Use rank + nullity = number of columns to analyse solvability and invertibility of a matrix.

concepts.name: Determinants
concepts.summary: Compute determinants by cofactor expansion or row reduction and interpret them as signed volume scaling and an invertibility test.

concepts.name: Orthogonality and projections
concepts.summary: Project a vector onto a line or subspace and relate orthogonal complements to row space and null space.

misconceptions.text: Any set of vectors that spans a space is a basis for it.
The column space of the row-reduced matrix is the same as the column space of the original matrix.
The determinant of A + B equals det A + det B.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
concepts.summary: Find eigenvalues from det(A - λI) = 0, compute eigenspaces, and interpret them as directions preserved by a transformation.

concepts.name: Gram-Schmidt and QR
concepts.summary: Build an orthonormal basis from independent vectors and use QR factorization to organise the result.

concepts.name: Least squares
concepts.summary: Solve inconsistent systems by projecting b onto the column space via A^T A x = A^T b and judge the fit.

concepts.name: Change of basis
concepts.summary: Represent a linear map in different bases and recognise that similar matrices share eigenvalues, trace and determinant.

concepts.name: Diagonalization
concepts.summary: Decide when a matrix is diagonalizable and use A = PDP^-1 to compute powers and understand dynamics.

concepts.name: Algebraic versus geometric multiplicity
concepts.summary: Compare multiplicities of an eigenvalue to diagnose defective matrices that cannot be diagonalized.

concepts.name: Spectral theorem for symmetric matrices
concepts.summary: Explain why symmetric real matrices have real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors and use A = QΛQ^T.

misconceptions.text: Matrices with the same eigenvalues are always similar.
Eigenvalues of a real matrix are always real numbers.

concepts.name: Singular value decomposition
concepts.summary: Derive and interpret A = UΣV^T for any matrix, linking singular values to A^T A and to the geometry of the map.

concepts.name: Low-rank approximation
concepts.summary: Evaluate truncated SVD as the optimal rank-k approximation and judge truncation levels for compression or denoising.

concepts.name: Pseudoinverse
concepts.summary: Construct the pseudoinverse from the SVD and use it to give minimum-norm least-squares solutions for any system.

concepts.name: Conditioning and numerical stability
concepts.summary: Assess how the condition number governs error amplification and choose stable algorithms such as QR or SVD over normal equations.

concepts.name: Jordan form and generalized eigenvectors
concepts.summary: Analyse defective matrices through Jordan blocks and explain their effect on matrix powers and exponentials.

concepts.name: Positive definite matrices
concepts.summary: Characterise definiteness through eigenvalues, pivots and quadratic forms, and connect it to optimisation and Cholesky factorization.

concepts.name: Modelling with spectral methods
concepts.summary: Design spectral models such as PCA or Markov steady states, choosing the decomposition that suits the problem.

misconceptions.text: Singular values are just the absolute values of the eigenvalues of A.
A small determinant means a matrix is ill-conditioned.
Solving least squares through the normal equations is always as accurate as using QR or SVD.
